name: traceCall_native_structLogs
note: Callee is an EOA, so structLogs is empty and the value that matters is the gas accounting. Steps are rendered one per line, as in the ERC20 scenario, so both goldens read the same way.

name: traceCall_erc20_callTracer
note: A CELO-token transfer routes through the token-duality transfer precompile. Locks how that precompile is represented as a call frame.

name: traceCall_erc20_callTracer_withLog
note: Token duality emits the ERC20 Transfer event from a native balance move; withLog pins that the event surfaces on the right frame.

name: traceCall_erc20_structLogs
note: Opcode-level trace of the token-duality path. Steps are rendered one per line: keeping the full per-step stack would make this golden ~10k lines and unreviewable, while the stack depth still moves whenever the opcode sequence does. Stack contents are covered by the prestate and callTracer goldens, and the sender's genesis balance by the call_cip64 scenario.

name: traceCall_erc20_prestateTracer
note: Full prestate is deterministic at the genesis block (the dev fee recipient, which prestateTracer would otherwise include as a random top-level key, is the zero address there). Contract bytecode is dropped so the golden stays reviewable; codeHash coverage lives in the celo-alloy serde tests.

name: traceCall_cip64_callTracer
note: CIP-64 with real gas prices, so the fee-currency debit and credit actually run. gasUsed here covers the fee currency's registered intrinsic gas.

name: traceCall_cip64_no_fees_callTracer
note: Same call with defaulted (zero) gas prices: exercises the exchange-rate lookup without a debit.

name: traceCall_cip64_prestateTracer_diff
note: The CIP-64 fee flow as a state diff: the fee-token balance the sender loses and the fee recipient gains. This is the assertion a mis-pinned exchange rate breaks — a liveness check would still pass.

name: traceCall_cip64_second_currency_callTracer
note: The second genesis fee currency is wired to a different oracle at a different rate; keeps a single hardcoded rate from satisfying every CIP-64 golden.

name: traceCall_state_override_callTracer
note: Unfunded EOA made solvent through stateOverrides; covers the override plumbing on the trace path.

name: traceCall_cip64_block_override_callTracer
note: Block overrides must be applied before the fee-currency context is captured, otherwise the CIP-64 debit runs against a different block env than the call does.

name: call_cip64
note: eth_call accepting feeCurrency: the balanceOf result is the sender's genesis native balance, read through token duality.

name: estimateGas_cip64
note: Binary-search estimate over the fee currency's intrinsic gas. Deterministic for a given estimator, so a golden — a moved value means the estimator or the intrinsic-gas surcharge changed, both of which are worth a review.

name: estimateGas_cip64_lowercase_key
note: op-geth binds the fee-currency key case-insensitively and clients rely on it; must equal the canonical-key estimate above.

name: createAccessList_cip64
note: The access-list path builds its own EVM; feeCurrency must survive the request conversion there too.

name: fillTransaction_cip64_defaults
note: The only coverage of `fill_cip64_fee_defaults` over the wire. A CIP-64 request omitting both fee fields must come back with them denominated in the fee currency -- op-geth's setLondonFeeDefaults, so 2 * base_fee_fc + tip_fc -- not with native wei values that the handler would then misread as fee-currency units. No signer is involved: the Celo fill runs before the delegation that `eth_sendTransaction` and `eth_signTransaction` need an unlocked account for.

name: simulateV1_native
filter: [.[] | {number, gasUsed, baseFeePerGas, calls: [.calls[] | {status, gasUsed, returnData, error, logs}]}]
note: The simulated block carries a wall-clock timestamp and derived hashes; compare the execution outcome and the synthesized block env instead.

name: simulateV1_cip64
filter: [.[] | {number, gasUsed, baseFeePerGas, calls: [.calls[] | {status, gasUsed, returnData, error, logs}]}]
note: Regression guard for the base-fee-check store gate: a CIP-64 call under the default validation=false must simulate rather than panic or be rejected.

name: simulateV1_cip64_validation
filter: [.[] | {number, gasUsed, baseFeePerGas, calls: [.calls[] | {status, gasUsed, returnData, error, logs}]}]
note: validation=true keeps the base fee and the balance checks live, so this is the variant where the CIP-64 debit is for a non-zero amount.

name: simulateV1_two_blocks
filter: [.[] | {number, gasUsed, baseFeePerGas, calls: [.calls[] | {status, gasUsed, returnData, error, logs}]}]
note: Two simulated blocks in one request: the second must start from the first's post-state while still resolving its own fee-currency context.

name: traceCallMany_two_bundles
note: Per-bundle fee-currency context capture: two bundles touching different currencies in one request.

name: trace_call_erc20
note: The parity namespace renders the same execution differently; token duality has to be representable in both.

name: trace_callMany_cip64
note: trace_callMany builds a fresh EVM per call; every call in the sequence must still use the context captured before the first one ran.
